light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

clips.text: Y esto es lo que queda. Rayado parejo, firme, y no suelta nada. Pasa la mano... áspero, como tiene que ser.
clips.action: Crouching, he runs his bare palm slowly across the new grooved cement, then lifts the hand to show it is clean, no dust, and knocks on the new floor with his knuckles.

clips.text: Y la otra mitad, así estaba todo. Antes de seguir, quiero responderte lo que más me pregunta la gente.
clips.action: He points back over the diagonal border at the old cracked half, pulls a face, then stands up and turns toward the friend who films.

clips.text: Primera pregunta, la de siempre: ¿eso aguanta, o se levanta en un mes? Y está bien que desconfíes, eh.
clips.action: He holds up one finger for 'first question', then crosses his arms and nods slowly, as if agreeing with a doubt.

clips.text: Porque si le echas solo agua con cemento encima del piso viejo, eso no aguanta. Se hace polvo y salta en placas.
clips.action: He uncrosses his arms and points down at a thin flaky crust on the old half, pushing it with the toe of his boot so it crumbles into powder.

clips.text: Lo que aguanta es una carpeta de verdad: cemento con arena, pegada con una lechada, sobre un piso limpio y mojado.
clips.action: He steps onto the new half and stamps twice on it with his boot, then counts on his fingers: one, two, three.

clips.line: Yo eso ya lo vi. Mi cuñado le echó cemento al patio, y al mes barría arenilla todos los días.
clips.who: the neighbour standing in front of the camera (the fourth reference image is his face)
clips.voice: in Spanish with a neutral Latin American accent, the gruff, amused voice of a 65-year-old man; the man in the foreground does NOT speak, he only listens
clips.action: The neighbour at the gate uncrosses his arms and mimes sweeping sand with one hand while saying his line, gruff and amused; the presenter in the foreground only listens.

clips.text: ¿Y sabes por qué? Porque se le secó rápido. El cemento necesita agua para endurecer, no solo para mezclarse.
clips.action: He nods toward the gate as if answering the neighbour, then turns back to the friend who films and taps the new floor with the toe of his boot.

clips.text: Si lo dejas al sol el primer día, el agua se va antes de tiempo, la superficie queda floja, y suelta ese polvillo.
clips.action: He points up at the sky and then fans his hand over the old floor as if heat were rising from it, then rubs two fingers together as if feeling dust.

clips.text: Segunda pregunta: ¿cuánto de cada cosa? Para la carpeta, una medida de cemento por tres de arena.
clips.action: He holds up one finger and then three fingers on the other hand, showing them side by side to the friend who films.

clips.text: Un balde de cemento, tres baldes de arena. No a ojo, no a pala: con el mismo balde, para que cada tanda salga igual.
clips.action: He picks up an empty black plastic bucket from beside the wall and holds it up, tapping its side, then sets it down.

clips.text: Y el agua, de a poco. Tiene que quedar como tierra húmeda: la aprietas en el puño, y no chorrea.
clips.action: He puts the bucket down and makes a squeezing fist with one hand, then opens it slowly as if showing damp earth.
